findings.title: rotation range shorter than 180 deg: few or no in-run Friedel pairs
findings.threshold: range < 180 deg means (almost) no in-run Friedel pairs; limiting only if the geometry was refined from the data AND fewer than 30 in-run pairs exist and the range is not set by the sample environment
findings.evidence: run.geom (omega_step, n_frames), predicted_crossings of all expected signed hkl with the run's refined U and geometry (pairs = unordered {h,-h} both crossing), run.obs for observed pairs
findings.action: The scan range is set by the sample environment (max_range_deg given): this is not a choice. Compensate with more orientations of the crystal (see 'next_setting') and a calibrant/standard crystal to fix the geometry, because without in-run mates the geometry rests on the orientation fit alone.
findings.gain: simulated (validation/real/PREREG_friedel_geometry.md, positive control): about 1500 pairs of a 360 deg scan give tx +-0.002 deg and wedge +-0.001 deg; about 100 pairs give +-0.01 deg. On the real L-alanine runs (170 deg, 35-57 in-run pairs) the pair estimates agreed with the orientation fit within 0.035 deg (INCONCLUSIVE by the registered rule).
findings.scope: Predicted pair counts are geometric (a crossing on the detector); observed counts are what survived integration. Pairs between different runs need the unknown relative rotation of the runs and are reported, not used.

findings.title: completeness below the bar on the geometric denominator only (the missing ones are the weak half)
findings.threshold: completeness n>=2 < 0.85 or n>=1 < 0.95 on the geometric denominator; limiting only if the strong half (calculated |F|^2 above the median) is also below 0.85
findings.evidence: enumerate_hkl to the detector d_min, Laue-unique classes (SpaceGroup.asu_representative), merged n from ctx.merged(); reachable = predicted_crossings of any run
findings.action: Most of the missing reflections do cross the Ewald sphere inside the scans but were not observed: they are weak, masked or crowded. Check the 'systematic_floor' and 'resolution_limit' findings before changing anything; a longer exposure helps only if the floor is counting-limited.
findings.scope: The denominator is geometric (everything the detector can see, intrinsically weak reflections included), so 100 % is not attainable; the strong-half figure uses calculated |F|^2 of the supplied crystal. Anomalous differences are not modelled: Friedel mates count as one reflection.

findings.title: one more run at a re-oriented crystal is predicted to add the most missing reflections
findings.threshold: recommended when completeness n>=2 is below 0.85 and one more run is predicted to bring at least 5 unique reflections to n >= 2
findings.evidence: predicted_crossings of the unique reflections below n = 2 (all signed equivalents) for the refined U of the widest run rotated by candidate rotations about the stage X and Y axes in steps of the option setting_step_deg (15 deg), midas_stress axis_angle_to_orient_mat, same geometry and omega range; a reflection's predicted new observations = its crossings in the extra run
findings.action: Re-orient the crystal by about 315 deg about the X (beam) axis of the rotation stage at omega = 0 (a goniometer tilt/chi or a re-mount) and collect one more run with the same scan. PREDICTED: it brings 75 of the 94 unique reflections below n = 2 to n >= 2 and reaches 60 not seen so far (a repeat of the old orientation: 53 and 45).
findings.gain: PREDICTED from geometry only (a forecast, not a measurement): every crossing on the detector is assumed to be observed, so the real gain is smaller by the fraction of weak or crowded reflections.
findings.scope: The sign and zero of the goniometer angle are those of the refined U of the first run in the stage frame; check the direction against your goniometer. Absorption by the environment at the new orientation, shadowing and collisions are not modelled.

findings.title: the data run out of signal before the detector edge: most of the expected reflections in the outermost shell were never detected
findings.threshold: the outermost of 6 equal-volume shells of the expected (accessible) classes has n>=1 completeness below 0.5; this overrides a high median I/sigma of the reflections that WERE observed
findings.evidence: n>=1 completeness by shell of the expected unique classes (coverage numbers, aperture-aware) against the merged data; median F2/sigF2 of the observed ones listed for comparison
findings.action: A longer exposure, a brighter beam, a lower background or a lower temperature raise the signal of the high-order reflections; more redundancy helps only if the floor is counting-limited (see 'systematic_floor'). The detector is not the limit here: it sees these reflections, the data do not contain them.
findings.scope: completeness here counts reflections that are intrinsically weak (heavy displacement, high order) as missing; a crystal that simply does not diffract that far gives the same finding.

findings.title: equivalents agree to counting statistics (floor 0.0%, counting 2.5%)
findings.threshold: limiting when f >= 8% and f / counting >= 2; note when only the ratio is exceeded. (the systematic floor f exceeds the counting-statistics prediction by this factor: more exposure no longer helps (L-alanine, A39: 14 % against 2.7 %, ratio 5); relative F2 floor above which equivalents disagree by more than a good data set does (L-alanine after the fixes: 5.9 %; before: 14.2 %))
findings.evidence: merge.systematic_floor on the merged observations (leave-one-out log deviation of symmetry equivalents, robust sd, minus the counting prediction); by L, d and run in measured
findings.action: The merged precision is counting-limited: more exposure or more redundancy improves it.
findings.scope: sees only what differs between equivalents; an error common to all equivalents (wrong cell in the Lorentz factor, absorption identical in every orientation) is invisible; says nothing about accuracy against a structure

findings.title: spots are sampled by only 0.5 frames (step 0.25 deg): the omega profile is barely resolved
findings.threshold: note when the median spot width is below 3 frames (undersampled profile) or above 30 frames (oversampled). (median spot width in frames below which the profile is sampled by fewer than about 3 frames (A39: median 1.3-2.4 at 0.2 deg))
findings.evidence: spots.omega_width_frames (the blob's extent in frames) of the blobs behind the observations
findings.action: a finer rotation step would resolve the profile: as a rule of thumb about a quarter of the spot width, here roughly 0.0297 deg (with a proportionally shorter exposure per frame); the total dose and scan time stay the same
findings.scope: the blob width in frames includes overlap and the finder's threshold; below about 2 frames it is an upper bound on the true angular width; the integrated intensity does not depend on the sampling, the profile shape and the crossing position do

findings.title: the rotation axis or detector is not where the header says: wedge up to 0.41 deg, tilt spread 0.03 deg, wedge spread 0.03 deg
findings.threshold: limiting when the orientation fit did not converge or its robust rms exceeds 2 px or 1 frame; note when the refined wedge, a tilt or their run-to-run spread exceeds 0.1 deg or a wavelength/cell scale had to be fitted. (wedge or tilt above this (or a run-to-run spread above it) means the axis or detector is not where the header says)
findings.evidence: Reduction.geom (refined) and Reduction.orientation of every run; the header values only when options['header_geometry'] is given
findings.action: the fit models this, so the merged data are not degraded by it; check the alignment of the rotation axis to the beam and the detector tilt at the beamline so that it is small to begin with, and use scans of 180 deg or more where possible: Friedel pairs inside a run then measure tx and the wedge without the orientation fit. No calibrant pattern is recorded for this data: measure one (CeO2 or LaB6) at the same energy and sample-detector distance, ideally before and after.
findings.scope: the geometry is refined from the spots themselves; a consistent run-to-run value does not prove it is right, and a calibrant is the only independent check
